text:
Casey Mittelstadt scored his 100th career goal, and he did it in a game Boston had no business making hard on itself. The Bruins trailed 3-2 in the third period against San Jose, then scored four times in about eleven minutes and won 6-4 at TD Garden.

Mittelstadt, drafted eighth overall by Buffalo in 2017, opened the scoring at 3:08 of the first. The Sharks answered on the power play through Michael Misa, and the game stayed tight until Dmitry Orlov's power-play slap shot put San Jose up in the third. David Pastrnak tied it on a 5% chance (our measure of how often a shot like that goes in), James Hagens scored 40 seconds later, and Fraser Minten and Will Borgen added the rest. Will Smith, the fourth pick in 2023, got one back for the Sharks in between.

The scoreboard made it look like a comeback, but our numbers say Boston controlled the game throughout. The Bruins out-attempted San Jose 65 to 43 and led in expected goals (the quality of chances created) 5.34 to 2.36. By our simulation of every shot, Boston deserved to win 85% of the time. Jeremy Swayman allowed 1.64 more goals than his shots deserved, which kept the Sharks in it, but Boston's shot volume was too much. Alex Nedeljkovic faced 34 shots and gave up five, about what the chances warranted.

Boston has now beaten San Jose twice this season, after a 6-3 win on Oct. 13. For the Sharks, it is another game that slipped away after they held a third-period lead.
